sources.name: OpenAI News
sources.note: Company announcements; about 2 a day. Press articles link here as the primary source.

sources.name: OpenAI Deployment Safety Hub
sources.note: System cards, one per OpenAI model launch, newest first. openai.com/index/* refuses the scanner (403), this host does not. One entry per scan so the first scan takes only the newest card, never the back catalogue.

sources.name: Google AI blog
sources.note: Google product and research AI announcements on blog.google.

sources.name: Google DeepMind blog
sources.note: Model and research releases; a few a week.

sources.name: Anthropic news
sources.note: No RSS feed; the news index page is read as an HTML listing. Model launches live at the site root (/claude-opus-5-5, /claude-sonnet-5-5), not under /news/, hence the second prefix (2026-09-30).

sources.name: Claude blog
sources.note: Anthropic's product posts (Claude apps, Claude Code, connectors); no RSS. Separate from anthropic.com/news, which carries company and model announcements. claude.com/blog moved in October 2026: it redirects to /resources/articles and every post is now /resources/articles/<slug>, so the old /blog/ prefix read nothing. The listing is the Product announcements category and not /resources/articles: on 2026-10-10 the two showed the same product posts, and half of what /resources/articles added was customer stories the writer would decline. Each card is one link whose text starts with the type and the date; the candidate takes the page's own title. The first card is a pinned older post, which a source's first scan records as seen (scanner.BASELINE); the listing shows about seven cards, so the default 20 entries per scan covers it.

sources.name: Claude Platform release notes
sources.note: Anthropic's API release notes. Every entry links to an anchor on one shared page, so the entry's feed summary (about 1,200 characters, the day's notes in full) is the evidence and revalidation reads the feed, not the page.

sources.name: Claude developer blog
sources.note: Anthropic's developer posts since July 2026 (Claude Code field guides, building with a new model, agent automations); a few a week, most of them how-to pieces the writer will decline as news. The story is div#body: the pages have no <article> or <main>, and without the id the page reads as empty (2026-10-10: 15,000 and 26,000 characters with it).

sources.name: Claude Code changelog
sources.note: One entry per Claude Code version, one or two a day, titled with the bare version number. Every entry links to an anchor on one shared page of 4.8 MB, over the fetcher's 2 MB cap, so the feed entry is the evidence; it sits in <content:encoded>, which feeds.parse_xml_feed reads when an item has no description. Twice a day and the top two entries only: most versions are lists of small fixes the writer will decline, and this keeps that to four candidates a day.

sources.name: Anthropic engineering
sources.note: Anthropic's engineering posts; shares its host with Anthropic news. Quiet since May 2026 (developer posts now go to claude.dev), kept for the occasional long piece. The listing shows all 25 posts, so the cap is 50 and not the default 20: with 20, removing one post would bring the twenty-first into view as an undated entry the scanner had never seen, and an old post would be read as new.

sources.name: Hugging Face blog
sources.note: Open-model releases; many posts are tutorials the writer will decline.

sources.name: NVIDIA blog
sources.note: AI and hardware announcements; the vertical is chosen per story.

sources.name: Apple Newsroom
sources.note: Apple product and platform announcements.

sources.name: Microsoft official blog
sources.note: Company announcements. The separate AI feed (blogs.microsoft.com/ai/feed/) answered 4xx on 2026-09-24.

sources.name: Ethereum Foundation blog
sources.note: Protocol upgrades and network announcements; low volume.

sources.name: CFTC press releases
sources.note: US derivatives regulator; most releases are not about crypto and are declined by the writer. SEC press releases were left out: their pages extract to a 248-character access notice.

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.note: Press; roughly 15 stories a day. The story is div.entry-content: <main> also holds the Related and Latest in AI cards with relative times and a rotating event promo, which re-render every half hour.

sources.name: Ars Technica AI
sources.note: Press; a few stories a day. The main feeds.arstechnica.com feed is refused by robots.txt.

sources.name: The Verge AI
sources.note: Press; the feed only carries the latest ten stories. The traffic-ranked Most Popular rail sits inside <article> (duet--layout--rail) and reorders several times an hour; More in AI and Top Stories are duet--layout--article-recirc.

sources.name: CoinDesk
sources.note: Press; much of it is market commentary, which the writer declines. The story is div.document-body: <main> also holds Latest Crypto News with relative ages and, now and then, Russian UI labels. premium-hide drops the live price chips inside paragraphs (BTC$83,034.73, sometimes in Russian number format), captions and the video slot.

sources.name: The Block
sources.note: Press; policy and industry coverage. Disabled 2026-09-30: every article page answers 403 (Cloudflare) to the scanner and to curl alike, so no story could be read; CoinDesk and Decrypt cover the same news.

sources.name: Meta Newsroom
sources.note: Meta's own announcements, Llama and AI products included; added 2026-09-26 at the owner's request.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning Blog
sources.note: Amazon's cloud AI launches; many posts are how-tos, which the writer declares not newsworthy.

sources.name: Microsoft Research blog
sources.note: Microsoft Research papers and model releases.

sources.name: Google Keyword blog
sources.note: All of Google's official blog (Android, Pixel, Search), wider than the AI section above; the same post from both feeds is an exact duplicate.

sources.name: Google Cloud blog
sources.note: Google Cloud announcements; the feed's articles live on cloud.google.com.

sources.name: GitHub blog
sources.note: GitHub's announcements, Copilot and developer AI tools included.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog
sources.note: GitHub's product changelog, read for Copilot only: the feed covers all of GitHub (ten entries, about three days), and five of the ten named Copilot on 2026-10-10. One page per entry, 2,500 to 3,000 characters. Shares its host with GitHub blog.

sources.name: Cloudflare blog
sources.note: Cloudflare's announcements and incident write-ups.

sources.name: SEC press releases
sources.note: US regulator; most releases are not about crypto and the writer declares those not newsworthy.

sources.name: Chainalysis blog
sources.note: On-chain research and hack reports; first-party for its own findings. The story sits outside <article> and <main>; those hold only the related-posts cards.

sources.name: Decrypt
sources.note: Press; a second website for crypto stories, which automatic publication can count.

sources.name: Taiwan MODA press releases
sources.note: 數位發展部新聞稿. The press-release list URL is a 404; the home page lists the five newest, newest first. Needs fetch.tls_context (TWCA chain fails Python 3.13's strict X.509 mode).

sources.name: Taiwan FSC press releases (crypto)
sources.note: 金管會新聞稿, only the crypto ones: most FSC releases are funds, insurance and statistics. The RSS page lists no feed URL; the news list page is read instead, news items told apart from the menu by their query string. maincontent keeps the release and drops the page's view counter, which would change the evidence hash on every fetch. Needs fetch.tls_context.

sources.name: Taiwan central bank press releases (crypto)
sources.note: 中央銀行新聞稿, only the crypto and digital-currency ones: most are monthly statistics. The RSS feed (rss-302-1.xml) is 3.4 MB, over the fetcher's 2 MB cap, so the 45 KB press-release list page is read instead; .cp is the release body. Needs fetch.tls_context.

sources.name: Taiwan NSTC press releases (technology)
sources.note: 國科會新聞資料, only technology titles (the list also carries humanities salons and visits). The RSS feed declares a DTD, which the XML parser refuses by design, so the news list page is read; #templateF is the release with its headline. Needs fetch.tls_context.

sources.name: Mistral AI news
sources.note: Mistral's own news feed (models, Le Chat, agents).

sources.name: Cohere blog
sources.note: No feed; the blog index is read as an HTML listing.

sources.name: Cursor blog

sources.name: Cursor changelog
sources.note: Cursor's release notes: two or three dated entries a month, one page per entry (2,500 to 7,000 characters). Shares its host with Cursor blog.

sources.name: Cognition blog
sources.note: Devin and Windsurf announcements; no feed.

sources.name: Replit blog

sources.name: Amazon news (AI)

sources.name: Stability AI news

sources.name: ElevenLabs blog

sources.note: Intel's press releases (investor relations feed).

sources.note: MediaTek's press-room feed.

sources.note: Lenovo's press-release index; no feed.

sources.note: ASUS press site feed.

sources.name: Ollama blog
sources.note: Ollama's announcements (new local models, app integrations, pricing): one to three dated posts a month, pages of 4,000 to 5,000 characters.

sources.name: OpenRouter announcements
sources.note: OpenRouter's product and model-availability posts. The blog index is read as an HTML listing and not through a feed, because only a listing can be narrowed to /blog/announcements/. The minimum title length is 14 and not 12 so the link to the category page itself ("Announcements", 13 characters) is not taken for a post.
